title: Enhancing nutritional management in peritoneal dialysis patients through a generative pre-trained transformers-based recipe generation tool: a pilot study.
summary: In a four-week self-controlled pilot of 35 peritoneal-dialysis patients, GPT-4 generated personalized meal plans reviewed by clinicians; serum prealbumin increased from 289.04 to 326.72 mg/L (p=.001), while albumin was not significantly changed and phosphate remained stable. Without a control group or systematic intake/adherence measures, the change cannot be attributed to GPT-4.
ai_technology: GPT-4 generated personalized renal meal plans from patient information; clinicians reviewed the menus before use.
organization: Department of Nephrology, Ren Ji Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, China; Department of Nephrology, Ningbo Hangzhou Bay Hospital, China; Molecular Cell Lab for Kidney Disease, Shanghai, China; Shanghai Peritoneal Dialysis Research Center, China; Uremia Diagnosis and Treatment Center, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, China; WORK Medical Technology Group LTD., China; Department of Medical Education, Ruijin Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, China

evidence.tested: After four weeks, mean serum prealbumin increased from 289.04 to 326.72 mg/L (p=.001); albumin did not significantly change and phosphate was stable.
evidence.unknown: Prospective self-controlled pilot of 35 patients over four weeks. No control arm; intake and adherence were not systematically measured, so the biomarker change cannot be attributed to the generated plans alone.
evidence.ai_role: The pilot measured a nutritional biomarker after GPT-4-assisted meal planning, but its design does not isolate an AI-specific effect.

source_review.scope: Primary full-text Methods, Results and limitations; publisher publication date checked.
